rationale: Matched-placebo fatigue results for NCT06298760 and PMID39642267 nigella-oil procedures remain unverified, and NCT07398885 has no available posted fatigue result. The historical attribution is secondary and has no measured effect.

Culinary clove is absent from the final scope. Published eugenol animal studies depend on administration route and timing and do not establish an effect of ingested ground clove on Parkinson rigidity.

Aging Lewy-body research used black pepper as a diagnostic odor. The human inhalation-source material does not report an improvement attributable to ingested ground pepper. Isolated mouse piperine studies address other behavior.

The clinical paper PMID42866378 and the registration disagree on allocation, blinding and timing. Its underlying analysis remains unavailable, as do results from completed topical trials IRCT20220403054396N1 and IRCT20241115063712N1.

NCT01216982 planned Epworth measurement with oral corn oil. Results and linkage to PMID24690964 remain unverified. The linked Parkinson cannabidiol vehicle and unrelated ethyl-ester comparison cannot isolate oral corn oil.

The odor identification comparison used sniffed dried caraway, finding 0 of 34 patients and 5 of 53 controls identified the odor. The study and its related odor-panel abstract do not measure change after eating toasted seed.

The archival lacquer-tree bark experiment concerns a different plant. Parkinson-derived fibroblasts and separate constituent studies supply no patient bradykinesia comparison for ground culinary sumac.

The primary body of PMID39588846 remains unresolved for cooking, assay, group sizes and cohort overlap. The accessible PMID39235924 used iron-exposed fly climbing, with conflicting group denominators and no postural clinical endpoint.

The atypical Parkinson source uses rocket for a standing sign. The bundled Parkinson menu reports aggregate motor scores and the isolated erucin experiment measures rotation in mice. Neither measures facial expression after raw arugula.
The historical proceedings mention the Laurel Rocket assay, not arugula. The human rocket-aroma record uses an odor stimulus, with no post-ingestion Parkinson olfaction measure.

Registry UMIN000056794 has no verified result for its registered paprika-extract fatigue measure, and UMIN000028271 registered fatigue but the available original reports respiratory outcomes. Other extract or constituent trials do not isolate raw bell pepper in Parkinson disease.
